stem: An investor with a risk-aversion coefficient of 3 evaluates a portfolio with an expected return of 11% and a standard deviation of 18%. Using U = E(r) − 0.5Aσ², the investor's utility is closest to:

rationale.A: Incorrect. 0.0128 omits the 1/2 in the utility function (0.11 − 3 × 0.0324).
rationale.B: Incorrect. −0.16 uses the standard deviation instead of the variance (0.11 − 1.5 × 0.18).

stem: The risk-free rate is 4%. A risky portfolio has an expected return of 12% and a standard deviation of 25%. For an investor with a risk-aversion coefficient of 3, the optimal proportion invested in the risky portfolio is closest to:

rationale.B: Incorrect. 10.67% uses the standard deviation instead of the variance in the denominator (0.08 / 0.75).

stem: A portfolio is 70% invested in Asset A (standard deviation 22%) and 30% in Asset B (standard deviation 10%). The correlation between A and B is −0.20. The portfolio standard deviation is closest to:

rationale.A: Incorrect. 18.40% is the weighted average of the standard deviations, valid only if correlation is +1.
rationale.B: Correct. Including the negative covariance term gives a variance of 0.022768 and σ = 15.09%.
rationale.C: Incorrect. 15.69% drops the covariance term entirely, as if correlation were zero.

stem: When a risk-free asset is available and investors share the same expectations, which statement is most accurate?
options: More risk-averse investors should choose a risky portfolio lower on the efficient frontier.
All investors hold the same optimal risky portfolio and differ only in how much they combine it with the risk-free asset.
Every portfolio on the minimum-variance frontier is efficient.
explanation: With a risk-free asset, the best CAL is tangent to the efficient frontier. Every investor holds that tangency portfolio and chooses their position on the line according to risk aversion (two-fund separation).

rationale.A: Incorrect. Risk aversion affects the mix with the risk-free asset, not which risky portfolio is chosen.
rationale.B: Correct. This is two-fund separation: one optimal risky portfolio, personal allocation to it.
rationale.C: Incorrect. Only the portion above the global minimum-variance portfolio is efficient.
